newsitem.title: USA: CME seeks to list Mexican interest rate products.
newsitem.headline: CME seeks to list Mexican interest rate products.

text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange said it filed for regulatory approval to trade futures and options on Mexican Treasury bills (CETES) and Mexican Equilibrium Interbank Rate (TIIE).
"Strong customer demand prompted the CME to consider offering Mexican interest rate products based on one- and three-month maturities," CME Chairman Jack Sandner said in a statement.
"And trading in CETES and TIIE contracts will complement the Merc's robust trade in Mexican peso futures and options," Sandner added.
The CETES contracts will be based on the 91-day CETES (Certificados de la Tesoreria de la Federacion), which are discount bills similar to U.S. T-bills, the exchange said.

The TIIE contracts will be based on the 28-day TIIE (Tasa de Interes Interbancario de Equilibrio), a rate determined by Banco de Mexico, Mexico's central bank, based on supply and demand for wholesale bank loans, CME said.

CETES futures will have a contract size of two million pesos, while TIIE contracts will be sized at six million pesos. A start date for trading will be set pending approval by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, CME said.

The new contracts will be part of CME's Growth and Emerging Markets (GEM) division, launched last year. The exchange already trades derivatives on the Mexican peso, Mexican par Brady bonds and the Mexican IPC stock index.
